headline: The building for Denmark’s quantum computer is finished. The computer is not.
dek: MAGNE’s Copenhagen facility cleared handover on 2 September; installation is only now beginning and full operation is expected in spring 2027. That makes a 2025 delivery promise measurable — and we just measured it.

source.name: The Quantum Insider
source.title: QuNorth Clears Facility Milestone for MAGNE Quantum Computer, 2 September 2026

body_html:
Ramboll has completed the specialised Copenhagen facility that will house MAGNE, the Atom Computing / Microsoft system bought by QuNorth — the Nordic initiative funded with €80 million from EIFO and the Novo Nordisk Foundation. The building has the vibration, temperature and magnetic-shielding control the machine needs. QuNorth can now begin installing. Full operation is expected in spring 2027.

This is a genuine milestone and also a quietly useful piece of evidence, because it dates something. In November 2024 Atom Computing and Microsoft announced a commercial machine with 24 entangled logical qubits, “available to order today with delivery in 2025”. MAGNE, specified at roughly 50 logical qubits on about 1,225 physical neutral atoms, is the system that sale became.

SymbiQ logged that 2024 announcement as a tracked claim with its resolution criteria frozen in advance — including, written before anyone looked, the rule that an order or a demo does not count; an operating delivered system does. This week's facility news is what settles it: the deadline was 31 December 2025 plus thirty days' grace, and as of September 2026 the machine is not yet installed. The claim now carries a drafted Not verified verdict awaiting a second reviewer. The full working is on the Ledger.

What this does NOT mean

  • Nobody was caught lying. Hardware schedules slip, and the original announcement was explicit that delivery was a 2025 plan. What the record shows is that a dated promise did not come true inside its own window — a statement about a claim, never about the people who made it.
  • A finished building is not a finished computer. Neutral-atom systems are installed, cooled, calibrated and characterised over months.
  • 50 logical qubits is a specification, not a measurement. No result from delivered hardware supports it yet, and the number to watch on arrival is the error rate, not the count.
  • This says nothing about whether the technology works. Atom Computing and Microsoft's 2024 logical-qubit entanglement result was real. Shipping a product on a date is a different problem from doing the physics.
concept_card_html:
Concepts in this story

Each of these is already explained on SymbiQ. Depth chips say how deep the explanation goes.

  • logical qubitplainOne reliable qubit built out of many unreliable ones. The only qubit count that means anything.
  • neutral atomworkingOptical tweezers holding thousands of identical atoms, with rearrangeable geometry.
  • quantum error correctionplainSpreading one fragile qubit across many so the machine can find mistakes without ever looking at the answer.
